The mirtverse workbench

Source: vignettes/workbench.Rmd
workbench.Rmd

The workbench is a point-and-click app for people who would rather not write R code. It runs the same functions you would call yourself, and it writes the R code for everything you do, so you can rerun the analysis later or learn R along the way.

library(mirtverse)
launch_workbench()

# or start with your own data already loaded
launch_workbench(my_data)

The eight steps

Tab What you do
1. Data Pick an example dataset or upload CSV, Excel, SPSS, Stata or RDS. Choose the item columns, enter an answer key to score multiple-choice items, and declare missing-value codes.
2. Explore Classical item statistics, Cronbach’s alpha and the total-score distribution.
3. Model Let mirtverse compare models and recommend one, or choose the item type and number of dimensions yourself.
4. Results Plain-language interpretation, item table with flags, parameters, all graphics, and item health cards.
5. Scores Person scores (EAP, MAP, ML or WLE) with standard errors, a CSV download, and the sum-score conversion table.
6. Response times Upload response times to fit the joint model and flag rapid guessing with the residual rule or the NT10, NT15 or NT20 normative thresholds.
7. Report & code Download the HTML report and the R script that reproduces the analysis.
8. Pipeline Run the data through the assessment pipeline’s intake and calibration checks, or load a pipeline saved from R. See the stage tracker, select flags to acknowledge, override or drop items, recalibrate, and download the pipeline and its report.

Sharing the app

The workbench is an ordinary Shiny app. To host it for colleagues or students, put this in an app.R file and deploy it to shinyapps.io or Posit Connect:

library(mirtverse)
workbench_app()

The workbench is a tool for doing an analysis. To show finished results to people who do not use R, build a dashboard instead: see Sharing results with a dashboard.
